tagline: Truth over narrative. Who's really in control, one story at a time.
definition: The SGS Index (short for Sovereignty–Globalism Spectrum) sizes up the news with one simple question: does this give more power to everyday people and independent countries, or does it hand more control to big global institutions? "Sovereign" means people and nations running their own lives. "Globalist" means decisions moving up to far-off, centralized bodies. Your personal freedom counts the most, because that's where real independence starts, not with how strong a government is. Each day's top stories get a simple label, from Extremely Sovereign, through Neutral, to Extremely Globalist.
about: I'm Joe, known as CreatorJoe on X (@TraderJoe541). I've been on X since 2017 talking about news and money, and I created the SGS Index.

I built it to cut through the noise. Instead of just reading headlines, I ask one question about every story: is power moving toward regular people and independent countries, or toward big, centralized, global control? I've updated the index more than twenty times since late 2025, and I post each update openly on X.

On the money side, I watch government debt, interest rates, sound money (things like gold, silver and Bitcoin that can't just be printed at will) and decentralization (spreading power out instead of keeping it in a few hands). I use AI to run backtests, which check how an idea would have played out in the past, and simulations to stress-test ideas before I trust them. Stay sovereign.

newsletter.name: The Sovereign Ledger
newsletter.pitch: Long-term investing doesn't change much day to day, so this letter doesn't either. Once a month, The Sovereign Ledger steps back from the daily headlines and asks: did the world move toward more independence or more central control? Which trends got stronger, which ones faded, and what could that mean for the big picture? Think government debt and interest rates, central banks and paper money that can be printed at will, sound money like gold, silver and Bitcoin, how much countries rely on others for energy and goods, and the shift toward technology that no single company or government controls. You'll also get my research notes: the ideas I'm testing and how I test them, using AI backtests (checks of how an idea would have done in the past) and simulations, including where they fall short. It's free, it comes once a month, and it's not financial advice.
